newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Cash-strapped Kremlin to start charging visitors.
newsitem.headline: Cash-strapped Kremlin to start charging visitors.

text.p: Visitors to the Kremlin, historic heart of the Russian state, will soon have to start paying to get in under a decree signed on Tuesday by President Boris Yeltsin.

Yeltsin's press service said the money would be used to fund repair and restoration work in the Kremlin, a huge medieval compound that contains beautiful domed churches and richly endowed museums as well as government offices.
Only World War Two veterans, pensioners and other special groups will be exempt from paying the entrance fee, it said.

All official receptions on the Kremlin grounds, which include the world-famous Red Square and the pleasant Alexandrovsky Garden, will require the personal consent of the president, the press service added.
The commandant of the Kremlin will decide how much visitors will pay, it said. It was not clear when the entrance fees would be introduced.
Yeltsin, who is recovering from heart surgery, is expected to resume work at his office in the Kremlin later this month.
